Commentary.Commentary: 182 to win for Kenya to keep their hopes alive of making it to the playoffs and subsequently, the 2020 WT20. Has the stand of 73 in just 32 balls for the 6th wicket taken that hope away? We shall find out after the break.

Stephan Baard is down for an interview. Baard says that the wicket is very good in general. Praises Kenya for bowling very well after the first 6 overs. On the total, says that the wicket is a bit tacky here and there but the bowlers need to adjust their lengths pretty quickly. Advises his bowlers to hit the deck a bit harder and his spinners to vary their bowling a little bit.

Williams targetted the skipper Ngoche in the 18th over and then went berserk in the 19th. Erasmus took a cue from him and went bonkers in the final over as Namibia reached a position of comfort from a position of doldrums. Rakep Patel was the only bowler who bowled all his 4 overs well, going for just 21 but no other Kenyan bowler was consistent enough to sustain the pressure.

Kenya started nicely with the ball, dismissing Davin cheaply but then Baard and Kotze started to attack. That pegged the Kenyans back. But once the fielding restrictions were lifted, the bowlers started to come into their own. The choke started to work and things started to slow down pretty steadily till Craig Williams came along.

Wow. What a finish. 57 runs in the last 3 overs. 45 of those came in the last 2. 25 came in the final over. What happened to Kenya? They had the game under control but have perhaps let it slip at the death.

HALF CENTURY FOR ERASMUS! But what is going on? Kenya look rattled. A short ball, around leg, Gerhard pulls this behind square leg and comes back for the second. Wait. He is not done yet. The throw comes in, a wild one, well over the keeper. Erasmus spots that and calls his partner for the third who is already two-thirds down. The fielder who backed up the throw, collects and throws it to the bowler and Erasmus would have been short. But the throw is a high one and the bowler has to leap to collect - but fumbles. Plenty of drama! NAMIBIA FINISH ON 181/5!
FREE HIT TIME!

NO BALL AND SIX! A high full toss, dipping a touch, Erasmus heaves this over mid-wicket for half a dozen! On looking at the ball in replays, it seems a harsh decision. That was not above the waist and was dipping. But Erasmus will not complain as he gets one more ball to complete his half century.
FOUR! Cracking shot. Backs away, waits for the ball to land and then pulls this behind square leg!
SIX! Terrific batting. Full and around off, Erasmus gets down and sweeps this massively over mid-wicket!
Outside off, Erasmus looks to swipe but misses.

FOUR! Nicely done! 50-RUN STAND IS UP in 28 balls! Landed outside off, Erasmus looks to play the reverse pull, is cramped for room, but still manages to beat short third man by delaying his shot a bit!

Oops! What was that? A slower ball, fuller in length, around middle and leg, Williams backs away to the leg side and attempts to hit but is months early into the shot. Stumbles and is hit on the pads. A quick leg bye taken.
Elijah Otieno to bowl the final over. 2-0-18-0 so far.
Full and outside off, Craig looks to sweep but gets hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards short fine leg and a leg bye is taken. 20 from the over, 32 from the last 2!
WIDE. Pressure on the bowler. Bowls this full and wide outside off, it is left alone.

SIX! That is just a wonderful cricket shot. 30 runs have come in the last 11 balls. 150 UP FOR NAMIBIA. This third 50 has come in just 29 balls. A full toss, around off, Williams gets down and sweeps it over mid-wicket!
FOUR! TONK! He has hit that very well. A low full toss, around middle, Williams bends low and hammers it straight back over the bowler for a boundary!
That's hit the batsman on his pads. They pick up a single. Leg bye given by the umpire.
SIX! That is a terrific stroke. Full and around off, Erasmus gets down and paddles this into the terraces at fine leg!

EDGED, FOUR, NO BALL! Multi-event delivery. Let us just change the order a bit because we shall describe as and how we got to know. We are all ready for the all-African contest. Stephan Baard and Nikolaas Davin will open for Namibia. Elijah Otieno will start off proceedings to Baard. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Dirk Nannes has a look at the track and says it is horrible. Compares it to a drain. Sees that patch between long shades of grass and says that it looks to be a difficult track to bat upon but there will be runs on offer.

Kenyan skipper, Shem Ngoche, says that he wanted to bat first but Erasmus did not allow them to do that. So now, he wants to chase well. Believes that the team is doing well and backs his side to maintain that. On him carrying on for a long time, Shem Ngoche smiles and says that Collins Obuya has been around much longer.

Scotland skipper, Gerhard Erasmus, says that he is looking to bat first as he feels runs on the board play a key role. On the team's position in the table, Erasmus says that the bowling has clicked but the batting has been inconsistent. Reckons that an all-round show is on the cards. On Namibia getting the better of Kenya in the African Qualifiers, Erasmus says that today is a different day.
Kenya (UNCHANGED Playing XI) - Irfan Karim(wk), Aman Gandhi, Dhiren Gondaria, Collins Obuya, Rakep Patel, Shem Ngoche(c), Sachin Bhudia, Nelson Odhiambo, Lucas Oluoch, Jasraj Kundi and Elijah Otieno.
Namibia (UNCHANGED Playing XI) - Stephan Baard, Nikolaas Davin, JP Kotze, Craig Williams, Gerhard Erasmus(c), JJ Smit, Zane Green(wk), Christi Viljoen, Jan Frylinck, Bernard Scholtz and Ben Shikongo.
TOSS - NAMIBIA HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO BAT FIRST.
This is a tussle between two evenly placed teams with Namibia faring slightly better on the batting front. Both sides have good bowling attacks, so it might not be a high-scoring encounter.

Right! Back refreshed? We are back because the next game in Dubai is upon us. Kenya take on Namibia in a clash which is a midfield fight. Both are on 4 points and will be itching to join Netherlands and Scotland on 6. If you missed, Papua New Guinea have become the first team to qualify for the playoffs. More importantly, they will feature in the 2020 WT20.
